title: "Clear" appears twice on key list in keyboard manager

status.label: Confirm duplicate Clear labels on current release
status.detail: The issue is marked reproducible: the key dropdown contains two different keys named Clear, and the reporter suggests labeling the numpad key.

judgment.rationale: The report describes two different key events with the same label, likely the Clear key and NumPad 5 with NumLock off. A collaborator added a screenshot, and the issue is marked Status-Reproducible. The report is from PowerToys 0.73.0, so current UI behavior is not known.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.73.0 and says the key list contains two entries named Clear for different keystrokes.
The reporter suggests renaming the numpad entry to Clear (Numpad), consistent with other Numpad labels.
A collaborator added a screenshot in the issue thread.
The issue is open and labeled Status-Reproducible and Priority-2; no linked fix was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether both duplicate labels remain on current stable; if they do, update the numpad label to distinguish the key events.

fix_assessment.rationale: If both entries remain indistinguishable on current builds, the numpad key should have a unique label consistent with other Numpad entries.

proposed_fixes.title: Give the Numpad Clear key a distinct label
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Two different key codes are presented as Clear in the selection list, leaving users unable to distinguish the dedicated Clear key from the NumLock-off Numpad 5 key.
plan: Confirm the duplicate labels remain in the current Keyboard Manager key list.
Identify which entry corresponds to the NumLock-off Numpad 5 key.
Rename that entry to Clear (Numpad) using the existing localization mechanism.
Add or update a test for distinct labels and key identities.
verification: Verify both Clear-related entries have unique, understandable labels.
Verify selecting each entry still maps the intended key code.
Verify the label is localized and consistent with other Numpad key names.

confidence.rationale: The issue gives a reproducible UI defect and a consistent label proposal; the only remaining check is whether it persists in current stable.
